summary: Christian Luczanits specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, earning his Magister (1994) and Ph.D. (1998) from the University of Vienna. He held positions at the University of Vienna, Lumbini International Research Institute, Stanford, UC Berkeley, and the Rubin Museum of Art.

Christian Wittern works in sinology and Buddhist studies, having studied under Seizan Yanagida. He held a professorship at Kyoto University (attested 1993, 2008) and a post at Hanazono University (attested 2011).

Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck (1866–1951) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leiden University (~1884–1888). He served on the faculties of the University of Amsterdam (1892–1899) and Leiden University (1899–1926).

Christine Chojnacki is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed her doctoral thesis at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 1991. She is attested as a professor at Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 in 2018.

Christine Mollier specializes in sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, having studied under Kristofer Schipper. She served as a researcher (1989–1995) and Director of Research at CNRS, and as a visiting professor at the University of Chicago.

Christof Zotter works in Indology and religious studies. In 2018, he is attested as head of the editorial program and postdoctoral researcher at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and as an editorial board member for Documenta Nepalica.

Christoph Anderl is a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned an MA from the University of Vienna (1995) and completed his PhD at the University of Oslo (~1999–2005) under Christoph Harbsmeier.

Christoph Cüppers is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg (~1974–1983) under Lambert Schmithausen, Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, and Albrecht Wezler. He served as Director of the Lumbini International Research Institute (~1993–2013).

Christoph Emmrich specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, completing his PhD at the University of Heidelberg in 2004. He held posts at the University of Heidelberg (attested 2001) and the University of Toronto as Assistant Professor.

Christoph Harbsmeier specializes in sinology and linguistics, having studied at Merton College, Oxford, and the University of Copenhagen (Ph.D.). He held posts at Universiti Sains Malaysia, the University of Oslo (Professor, 1980), Peking University, Fudan University, and Shanghai Normal University.

Christoph Kleine is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who earned his degrees, including PhD and Habilitation, at the University of Marburg. He held posts at Marburg, EFEO, Hōbōgirin, the University of Munich, and Leipzig University.

Christoph Theodosius Walther (1699–1741) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied theology at the University of Halle (1720). He served as a missionary with the Danish-Halle Mission from ~1725 to 1739.

Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf (1909–1995) studied anthropology at the University of Vienna and the London School of Economics, under Leo Frobenius and Robert von Heine-Geldern. He held professorships at Osmania University, SOAS, the University of London, and UCL.
Christophe Jaffrelot is an Indologist who studied at Sciences Po (~1987–1991) under Jean Leca. He held posts at Sciences Po and CNRS starting around 1991.
Christophe Vielle is an Indologist attested as a professor of Sanskrit (2009) and professor (2013) at the Université catholique de Louvain.

Christopher Byrne specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at McGill University (attested 2015), where he studied under Grace S. Fong, G. Victor Sōgen Hori, and Robin D. S. Yates.
Christopher D. Emms works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his studies at McMaster University under the supervision of Shayne Clarke (attested 2012).

Christopher G. Framarin is an Indologist and philosopher who earned an M.A. from the University of Hawaiʻi (2001) and a Ph.D. from the University of New Mexico (2005). He became an associate professor at the University of Calgary (attested 2014).
Christopher Hatchell specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Virginia, where he was mentored by David F. Germano.

Christopher I. Beckwith works in Tibetology, linguistics, and Central Asian studies, holding degrees from Ohio State and Indiana University, where he studied under Helmut Hoffmann and Thubten Jigme Norbu. He held posts at Indiana University, including editor in 1982.
